catholic-encyclopedia-1913-william-herin:
William Herincx was a Flemish Franciscan theologian whose Summa shaped his order's schools. Born at Helmond in 1621, he died on 17 August 1678. After schooling at 's Hertogenbosch, he read classics at Louvain with ardour, took a philosophy doctorate, and entered the Franciscans. In 1653 he began lecturing in theology at Louvain, and in 1658 his superiors charged him with drafting a theology course for Franciscan schools, its first volume appearing in 1660.

Herincx taught that theology must seek truth for holiness, kindling love of God in teacher and pupil alike. He followed Duns Scotus while drawing on Bonaventure and Thomas, and his tract on conscience stands as a masterwork on probabilism, the view that a probable opinion may guide action. Twice provincial minister and later commissary general, he was named Bishop of Ypres in 1677 and died during his first visitation, less than a year later.
